Subject: Request: carveout for streaming TTF / sustained tokens for investigator UI

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our fraud investigations UI is moving into a closed pilot and the engineering team ran an early integration with Redwood streaming endpoints. Two behaviors popped up that procurement/legal want captured before we sign:

- Time-to-first-token (TTF) for streaming sessions occasionally spikes to ~300–400ms during traffic surges (pilot shows this at ~5% of sessions).
- Sustained per-session token output rate drops under high concurrency; our workflow needs ~30 tokens/sec sustained for an interactive transcript experience.

We understand hosted conditions vary, but BrightBank requires a written SLA carveout or alternative commitment describing expected variability and remediation/credits. Specifically:

1) Can Redwood commit to a TTF p95 for streaming sessions (or provide a clear exception we can accept)?
2) Can you define a sustained tokens/sec expectation per connection and what mitigations you offer when that falls below the target?
3) What telemetry and runbook will you share if we hit degradations?

I've attached a sample traffic extract (BrightBank_traffic_sample.csv) and a suggested contract template for exceptions (BrightBank-sla-exception-template.docx). Procurement would like a short written response we can include in the SOW.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants language by Friday EOD.

Samira

Kim / Team —

On Wed, Jul 7, 2026 at 10:02 AM kimberly.park@redwood.ai wrote:
> Samira —
> 
> Thanks for the detailed note and the sample traffic. Appreciate the deadline — we'll prioritize.

I've reviewed the sample traffic and run a couple of microbenchmarks against the model family BrightBank selected (redwood-open-2.7B q4_0). High-level findings:

- Baseline streaming TTF (warm) on our hosted pool: ~60–90ms median, ~130–160ms p95.
- Under concurrent spikes that cause batching window growth and cold KV cache misses, p95 can slip into the 300–450ms range for a small fraction (~3–7%) of sessions. That aligns with Samira's observations.
- Sustained per-session token throughput depends on batching and CPU/GPU scheduling: on shared pools we've observed 20–50 tokens/sec per session, with variance tied to concurrent active sessions and request arrival patterns.

Options to meet BrightBank's ask:
1) Dedicated warm pool (pinned instances) — we can guarantee lower variance. Estimated additional cost: reserved Dedicated tier.
2) Pre-warm strategy + small initial unbatched window — reduces TTF spikes but increases unit cost slightly.
3) Explicit per-session token-rate SLO with a documented mitigation: if sustained token-rate falls below agreed threshold, Redwood will (a) activate temporary pinned throughput for affected sessions, (b) notify BrightBank via the monitoring webhook, and (c) issue service credit if remediation misses SLA.

Recommended practical carveout draft for Sales/Legal to consider (technical text):

"Redwood will target a Time-to-First-Token (TTF) of <= 200ms p95 for streaming endpoints under the traffic profile provided by BrightBank (defined in Attachment A). In periods where shared-hosted pool conditions cause transient TTF degradation, Redwood will either (i) notify BrightBank and invoke a pre-agreed mitigation (warm-pool activation) within 15 minutes, or (ii) shift affected traffic to a compatible non-streaming endpoint with equivalent model variant. If Redwood fails to remediate within the agreed window, service credits will apply per Section X."

For token-rate: propose: "Redwood will commit to a sustained token-rate of >= 30 tokens/sec per active streaming session p95 under the agreed concurrency envelope. If sustained throughput falls below the threshold for a sustained window of 120 seconds, Redwood will follow the mitigation steps above."

I'll attach a short SLO draft (slo-draft-v1.pdf) for Marissa/Legal and can iterate quickly. Also note that any firm SLA for hosted will require us to bind the traffic envelope (peak RPS, session average token count) and possibly a Dedicated commitment.

Rishi

Samira —

Thanks for your patience. Below is the carveout language Redwood can accept for the SOW given the traffic profile you shared. This is intentionally prescriptive so procurement can paste it into the SOW and procurement/legal can iterate if needed.

Proposed SLA carveout (draft):

1) Scope & Traffic Envelope: BrightBank will provide a representative traffic profile (Attachment A). The guarantees below apply only within that envelope. Any sustained increase in peak concurrency or session token volume beyond Attachment A requires a re-evaluation of the commitments and possible Dedicated deployment.

2) Time-to-First-Token (Streaming): Redwood will target a Time-to-First-Token (TTF) <= 200ms p95 for streaming endpoints using the model variants specified in Attachment B when operated within the agreed traffic envelope. During transient conditions on shared-hosted pools that cause TTF degradation, Redwood will:
   a) Notify BrightBank via monitoring webhook and email within 5 minutes of detection.
   b) Invoke pre-agreed mitigation (warm-pool activation or pinned throughput) within 15 minutes.
   c) If remediation is not completed within 60 minutes, BrightBank will be eligible for a service credit per the SOW credit table.

3) Sustained Token-Rate (Per-session): Redwood will commit to a sustained per-session token-rate >= 30 tokens/sec p95 under the agreed concurrency envelope. If sustained throughput falls below 30 tokens/sec for a continuous 120-second window, Redwood will:
   a) Notify BrightBank and initiate mitigation (as above).
   b) Offer temporary pinned capacity or route affected sessions to a compatible non-streaming endpoint until normal throughput resumes.

4) Telemetry & Runbook: Redwood will provide access to a monitoring webhook, a daily incident digest during active remediation, and a post-incident report outlining root cause and corrective actions.

5) Credits & Escalation: Service credit triggers and escalation paths are defined in Attachment C.

Next steps:
- If BrightBank accepts this draft, Legal/Procurement can paste into the SOW and sign the DocuSign link below.
- For production stability we recommend starting the pilot on a Dedicated warm-pool for the first 30 days and then evaluating whether hosted carveout is acceptable.

DocuSign (SOW exception): https://docusign.com/tx/7f3a2b
Tracking ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-4312
